title: Dedicated: autoscaler burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: customers with Dedicated fleets asked for better short-term bursting behavior and stronger throughput guarantees without sacrificing long-term utilization. This PR implements burst controls for the Dedicated autoscaler, introduces a lightweight throughput-guarantee flag for fleets, and extends utilization reporting to support 1m/5m aggregates and per-fleet burst consumption metrics. Summary of changes: - Autoscaler: add burst_capacity and burst_window_ms config fields; implement token-bucket based burst admission in the fleet autoscaler; ensure graceful degradation when burst budget is exhausted. - Throughput guarantees: add 'min_reserve_qps' and 'guarantee_policy' (strict/elastic) on fleet configs to reserve baseline RPC capacity for critical tenants. - Utilization reporting: new metrics (fleet_utilization_1m, fleet_utilization_5m, burst_budget_remaining, burst_consumption_rate) emitted from autoscaler and aggregator; Console: per-fleet dashboard panels and alerts. - CLI/Controller: new validation and migration path for existing fleet configs. - Tests: unit and integration tests for admission behavior and reporting; stress tests validating burst admission up to 3x baseline for short windows. Backwards compatibility: default for new fields is conservative (burst disabled, no reserve). Existing fleets will be unchanged unless updated by operators. Rollout plan: canary on 2 internal Dedicated fleets in us-west for 48h, observe utilization and latency regressions, then staged rollout across all Dedicated fleets. Linear: ENG-2145 (burst controls), ENG-2201 (utilization reporting). Release notes attached. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Canary run - [x] Docs updated (console + API) Implementation notes: burst admission uses a leaky/burstable token-bucket with conservative replenishment rates derived from fleet provisioning sizes. To avoid noisy scaling, autoscaler only uses burst admission when the target scaling decision would otherwise have increased latency beyond SLO for >30s. We added telemetry counters to track burst hits and denied bursts for future tuning. Performance: canary fleets showed 2.8x short-term throughput improvement for spike load while median latency stayed within 5% of baseline. No observable long-term cost increase. Migration: operators can opt-in to burst and/or min_reserve_qps via the fleet update API or via the Console. See docs/DEDICATED_AUTOSCALER.md for config examples and recommended guardrails.

release_notes: Dedicated: added autoscaler burst controls (burst_capacity, burst_window_ms) allowing short-term throughput spikes without immediate long-term scaling.
Dedicated: introduced throughput guarantees (min_reserve_qps + guarantee_policy) to reserve baseline capacity for critical workloads.
Observability: new utilization metrics (fleet_utilization_1m, fleet_utilization_5m, burst_budget_remaining, burst_consumption_rate) and Console dashboards/alerts.
Operators: burst and guarantee settings are opt-in; default behavior unchanged. See docs/DEDICATED_AUTOSCALER.md for migration and examples.
